## A candidate on the entire source family

Write A(i,j) for the literal source coefficient at reduced a/b, and put
N=b-1 and s=i+j-a. Polygon membership implies 0<=s and s+2<=N for a
horizontal triple. The proposed stronger inequality is

    (s+2)(N-s) A(i,j) A(i+2,j)
      <= (s+1)(N-s-1) A(i+1,j)^2.

Equivalently, the horizontal coefficients divided by choose(N,s) should be
log-concave, with s changing along the row. This normalization is an auxiliary
sufficient condition, NOT the pinned target. The two scalar factors differ
by N+1=b. Nonnegative source coefficients and positive right scalar therefore
give the original raw inequality. MarkovAmbient77c2 proves this implication
with the actual polygon hypotheses and raw coefficients. AmbientHorizontal77
is a Prop definition and is not asserted as a theorem.

This extends the preceding Pell candidate from ambient a for a/(a+1) to
ambient b-1 for every source. It does not replace the other two directions.

## Unconditional first-row calculation

For c_k=[x^k](1+x)^n(A+Bx), A,B>=0, put N=n+2. The exact identity is

    c_k / choose(N,k+1)
      = (k+1)[A(n+1-k)+Bk] / ((n+2)(n+1)), 0<=k<=n+1.

The numerator has shape f(s)=s(C+Ds). At consecutive indices,

    f(s+1)^2-f(s)f(s+2)
      = [C+D(s+1)]^2 + D^2 s(s+2).

This is nonnegative for s>=0, including decreasing affine factors and zero
cases. The generic proof and binomial normalization identities are checked
in MarkovRowNormalization77c2. The source first-row identity already proved
in MarkovHorizontalLCB46 is

    [v]P_(a/b)=u^a(1+u)^(b-3)[(3a-1)+(a+b-1)u].

The new exact source bridge gives the ambient normalized inequality on j=1
for every path. Polynomial mapping and shifting are checked explicitly.
MarkovAmbientScaling77c2 converts normalized comparisons to their literal
integer-scaled form using the exact binomial ratio identity, without assuming
that the source coefficients are nonzero. Polygon membership on j=1 forces
i>=a, so this covers every admissible horizontal triple in that row.

## Entire numerator-one family

For the source 1/b, set N=b-1 and s=i+j-1. The exact Fibonacci formula and
the elementary binomial subset identity give

    A(i,j)/choose(N,s)
      = choose(s,j) choose(s+1,j)/choose(N,j), i>=1.

For fixed j each numerator factor is log-concave as its upper argument
increases. Their product is log-concave, so the stronger ambient inequality
holds for the entire numerator-one horizontal family. The binomial identity,
normalization, inequality and conversion back to integer scalars are checked
in MarkovFibonacciAmbient77c2. MarkovAmbientSourceBounds77c2 supplies the exact
source and polygon transports when its successful receipts are listed in the
validation manifest. No statement about general interior rows follows.

ambient-source.json records 824,919 raw horizontal tests on all reduced
interior rationals of denominator <=50, with no ambient failure. The 342,074
coefficientwise tests using the earlier common C-site parameter, restricted
to denominator <=24, DO have a failure. At source 2/7, row j=1, i=5,6,7,
the deformed coefficients are experimentally

    64+4t, 36+t, 8.

The scaled gap is 336-24t+5t^2. Its coefficient of t is negative (-24),
but its value is positive for every real t, since

    5(336-24t+5t^2)=(5t-12)^2+1536.

At the actual source t=1 the raw triple is [68,37,8]; its raw gap is 825 and
its scaled gap is 317, both positive. These source-deformation identifications
are finite Python evidence here, not new Lean theorems. The refinement is
different from the inherited Pell charge q. Failure of one coefficientwise
refinement does not refute either unrefined candidate.

ambient-weights.json additionally records 1,365,665 exact evaluations at
t in {0,1,2,5,10,100,1000} for the 383 reduced source words with denominator
<=35. No ambient failure was found. Only t=1 is the actual source family.
All scans preserve zero coefficients by lookup with default zero; zero
endpoint products are omitted from counted nontrivial tests because their
inequality follows from a nonnegative middle square.

## Pell generating-function route retained as a derivation

For inherited H(a,j,s,q)=choose(a-q,s)choose(s+q-1,q)choose(2s,j-q),
s>=1, negative-binomial expansions give the formal generating identity

# Vertical top-face inequalities and transfer obstructions

Machine-authored request b5dbe087bddc41aaa420318d5cb776a1. No novelty claim.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. Formal validation is recorded
separately; finite experiments do not establish universal statements.

For source a/b let d=a+b−1, N=b−1, B=a−1 and D=i+j=d−2.
Write L=A(i,j), M=A(i,j+1), R=A(i,j+2), F=choose(D,i). The inherited
homogeneous layer formulas, with the new vertical middle coefficient bridge, give

    (j+1)M = F[B(j+1)+Ni],
    (j+1)(j+2)R = (D+1)(D+2)F,
    2D(D−1)L = TF,
    T=N(N−1)i(i−1)+2(BN+N−3B−1)ij+B(B−1)j(j−1).

We have N+B=D+1, B≥0 and N≥B+1. For D≥2 the raw gap clears to

    2D(D−1)(j+1)²(j+2)(M²−LR)=F² G,
    G=2D(D−1)(j+2)[B(j+1)+Ni]²−(j+1)(D+1)(D+2)T.

The generator expresses (2D)²G as a positive polynomial in nonnegative
variables i−2,j,2B,D−2B for i≥2. Separate certificates use j−1 for i=1
and j−2 for i=0. There are 101, 19 and 15 nonzero monomials respectively.
Lean checks the identities by ring normalization and their signs by order
reasoning, then cancels only the strictly positive displayed factor.

The source theorem source_top_vertical_rawB5 covers every path and every
polygon triple ending on the top face. Small degrees force a=1 and use the
inherited full numerator-one theorem. Thus no small case, zero coefficient or
endpoint is dropped. The large-degree algebra even covers the displayed
nonnegative index positions without a polygon assumption.

The constant one in this raw vertical inequality is optimal uniformly across
sources. For path replicate(j+1,false), corresponding to 1/(j+3), the valid
top-ending vertical triple at i=1 has coefficients [j+1,j+2,j+3]. Its gap is
exactly 1. For any real c>1 an Archimedean choice of j makes
c(j+1)(j+3)>(j+2)². vertical_uniform_constant_sharpB5 proves this with
actual source coefficients and all three polygon guards. This is an obstruction
to a strict uniform multiplicative strengthening, not to raw log-concavity.

Combining the new vertical theorem with inherited horizontal and diagonal
theorems gives root_iff_interiorB5. Its residual Interior63B5 retains all
paths and all three polygon guards. The remaining horizontal and vertical
triples have i+j+3≤d; the remaining diagonal triples have i+j+5≤d.
Equivalently, it removes exactly the triples wholly contained in the top
three homogeneous layers. Both directions and both endpoint clauses are
checked. The residual proposition remains unproved and infinite.

## Global invariant investigation

Using the exact two-state affine transfer, the script tests ULC in s with
ambient degree N=word length+1 separately for f, g and F=yf+g, and tests
adjacent minors in (s,j). All words of length≤10 were enumerated. The
individual-state ULC hypotheses fail, for example g on AAAB has row triple
[2,11,32] at s=1,j=2 and scaled gap −42. Source-word scans are kept separate
because these arbitrary words are not automatically source central words.

For actual sources through denominator 45, the TP2 candidate fails already
for 8/9. Its ambient entries C(1,6), C(2,6), C(1,7), C(2,7) are
[12,464,8,296], with determinant −160. No pinned three-point inequality is
reversed by this four-position minor.

The inherited exact Pell formulas yield a universal expression. On path
replicate(k+j,true), with j≥4, the determinant formed from raw positions
(k+2,j),(k+3,j),(k+1,j+1),(k+2,j+1) is

    32[(k+2)³−j((k+2)²−(k+2)−1)−2].

For k=0 it equals 32(6−j), strictly negative for every j≥7. All four
positions are in the actual source polygon. In ambient coordinates this is
C(1,j)C(2,j+1)−C(2,j)C(1,j+1). The universal formula and its exact source
and ambient interpretation are checked in MarkovShearObstructionB5 if listed
as successfully validated in the final manifest.

The palindrome scan tested 8,189 words of length≤22, retaining coefficient
zeros. Neither individual-state nor terminal-sum ambient ULC failed in its
8,860,294 recorded checks. This suggests a stronger palindrome-specific
induction hypothesis but proves none. Palindromic gas words already have a
checked sum-of-squares representation in MarkovSquares28b1; that inherited
result is not rediscovered or credited as new here.

A direct form in the newer ambient coordinates is useful for that proposed
induction. Both affine transfer matrices share

    K(x) = [[1+x,−x],[−x,x]],
    K T_A = [[xy,0],[0,x]],
    K T_B = [[y+xy²,xy],[xy,x]].

For Q_w(p,q)=(p,q)K T_w(p,q)^T, the exact sandwich identity is
Q_(r w r)(p,q)=Q_w(T_r(p,q)^T). Its central cases are

    Q_empty=p²+x(q−p)²,
    Q_A=x(yp²+q²),
    Q_B=yp²+x(yp+q)².

The source seed (p,q)=(x(1+y),1+x(1+y)) satisfies Q_w=xF_w.
MarkovAmbientFormB5 checks these identities over every commutative ring and
connects the seed expression to every source path without division by x.
These identities alone do not establish log-concavity or a preserved
coefficient inequality. They are a direct-coordinate form of the inherited
square structure, not a claimed new general sum-of-squares theorem.

The mixed term needed to combine the two state rows is a distinct obligation.
At ambient degree N, put A=(s+2)(N−s), B=(s+1)(N−s−1),
f_k=[x^(s+k)y^(j−1)]f (zero if j=0), g_k=[x^(s+k)y^j]g.
The terminal gap decomposes exactly as

    B(f_1+g_1)²−A(f_0+g_0)(f_2+g_2)
      =(B f_1²−A f_0 f_2)+(B g_1²−A g_0 g_2)
        +2B f_1g_1−A(f_0g_2+g_0f_2).

Even for palindromes the mixed term alone need not be nonnegative: word
ABBBBBBBBBA, s=1,j=9 has f=[0,10,524], g=[4,170,3692] and mixed gap
−1168. The total gap remains nonnegative in the tested cases. This arbitrary
palindrome is not silently identified with a source word. All-source mixed
nonnegativity is a separate candidate, still unproved. The exact tests and
their bounds are in synchrony.json and source-mixed-stress.json.

The final stress completed all 84 selected reduced fractions, with denominator
at most 120, testing 821960 triples for each of the two component gaps, the
mixed gap and the terminal gap. No failure occurred. Inputs and seed are saved;
these selected inputs are not exhaustive rational coverage. The palindrome
ULC test counts only existing left coefficients; when the left coefficient is
zero the tested inequality follows directly from the nonnegative square and
nonnegative scalar weight. Internal and right coefficient zeros are retained.
# Positive ambient transfer and the Pell kernel

Machine-authored request 5c90b5063976426b9c5577badcc55c00. No novelty claim.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. Formal status is determined
by the final validation manifest, not by the existence of a draft file.

## Exact all-source change of exponents

Set u=x, v=xy. For the source a/b let c be its inherited exact central A/B
word (length b-2, B-count a-1). The new denominator-free gauge calculation
proves

    P_(a/b)(x,xy) = x^a F_c(x,y),
    F_c = (y,1) T_c (x(1+y), 1+x(1+y))^T,
    T_A = [[xy,x],[xy,1+x]],
    T_B = [[y+xy(1+y),x(1+y)],
           [2y+xy(1+y),1+x(1+y)]] .

Both transfers are linear in x with nonnegative coefficients. Their linear
parts are H and (1+y)H, where H=[[y,1],[y,1]] and H^2=(1+y)H.
The constant parts are D_A=[[0,0],[0,1]] and D_B=[[y,0],[2y,1]].
This is an exact polynomial identity at x=0 as well: the proof multiplies
through the diagonal gauge and cancels only the nonzero polynomial X, never
a real value or a raw coefficient.

For s=i+j-a >=0 the literal coefficient identity is

    A(i,j) = [x^s y^j] F_c.

With i,j natural and i+j=a+s, the polygon condition is exactly

    s <= b-1,  (b-a)j <= b s.

The natural original index also retains j<=a+s. The three original
directions become respectively (1,0), (1,1), and (0,1) in (s,j). In
particular, a horizontal-only argument in these new variables does NOT
establish the original vertical or diagonal clauses.

## A broader sufficient horizontal target

For an arbitrary A/B word w let N=length(w)+1 and C_w(s,j)=[x^s y^j]F_w.
The proposed assertion is

    (s+2)(N-s) C_w(s,j) C_w(s+2,j)
       <= (s+1)(N-s-1) C_w(s+1,j)^2,   s+2<=N.

The new reduction connects this explicitly unproved all-word assertion to
the actual source ambient bound and hence raw horizontal inequalities.
It does not assume arbitrary-word vertical or diagonal log-concavity.

The exact enumeration extends earlier no-adjacent-C experiments to the
ambient bound: 28,656 gas cores of length 1 through 21, beginning and ending
in A and with no CC, give 4,415,699 nontrivial horizontal triples without
failure. Every such core is expand(w)A for a unique original A/B word w.
Zero endpoint products are omitted only from the nontrivial count; they
satisfy the tested inequality because all coefficients and both scalar
weights in range are nonnegative. This is finite evidence, not a proof.

## Exact Pell generating kernel

For c=B^(a-1), write Q_a=F_c and Q_0=1. The new formal recurrence is

    Q_1=1+x(1+y)^2,
    Q_(a+2)=(1+y+x(1+y)^2)Q_(a+1)-y Q_a.

As an ordinary formal power series in z, it gives the checked equation

    [(1-z)(1-yz)-xz(1+y)^2] sum_(a>=0) Q_a z^a = 1-yz.

The exact source coefficient bridge retains every natural i,j,s satisfying
i+j=a+s. This supplies the source interpretation of the ambient kernel.
The recurrence also gives the checked Cassini identity

    Q_a Q_(a+2)-Q_(a+1)^2 = x y^(a+1)(1+y)^2.

Its sign concerns the FAMILY index a, not any pinned coefficient direction.
It must not be used as a coefficient log-concavity assertion.

Writing K_s(z)=sum_(a>=0) [x^s]Q_a z^a, the extracted recurrence is

    (1-z)(1-yz) K_(s+1) = z(1+y)^2 K_s,
    (1-z) K_0 = 1.

MarkovAmbientSlices5c90 proves these equations over every commutative ring,
then proves by induction the denominator-cleared form of

    sum_(a>=s) [x^s]Q_a z^a
      = z^s(1+y)^(2s)/[(1-z)^(s+1)(1-yz)^s].

The extracted identity is therefore checked as an ordinary formal-power-series
equation, including s=0, with no division or convergence assumption. Its
positive binomial expansion is compatible with the inherited exact binomial
sums. None of these identities proves the aggregate coefficient inequality;
global horizontal aggregation remains open.

## A source obstruction to a tempting shortcut

For c=A (actual source 1/3), the new exact identity is

    F_A(x,y)=1+2x(1+y)+x^2(1+y)^3.

At y=1 this is 1+4x+8x^2, strictly positive for every real x and of degree
two. Thus even the sheared total-degree polynomial need not be real-rooted.
The exact source identity and strict positivity are proved in Lean; the
Sturm probe independently records zero real roots. This rules out blanket
real-rootedness of F_w(x,y) at positive y. It does not refute either the
ambient coefficient bound or the published raw inequalities. In particular,
evaluating y=1 sums many coefficient rows, whereas the horizontal target
extracts one fixed y coefficient.

An additional independent implementation of the two new transfers checked
2,047 full polynomial identities against the earlier gas representation,
then tested 200 seeded words of lengths 20,40,60,100 with various B densities.
Across all 2,247 words there were 929,901 nontrivial ambient inequalities and
no failure. The random words, seed 590, and exact counts are retained in
ambient-transfer.json. These tests also verified the constant x coefficient
1 and top x coefficient (1+y)^(length(w)+count_B(w)+2) on those words only.

## Operational evidence

The immediate predecessor completed and all 62 changed research/evidence
hashes match its receipt. No side effect was replayed. Earlier interrupted
work was already reconciled by completed successors. Higher-priority
permissions prohibit .scratch reads; durable research/evidence paths were

Hosted primary-source reading used the published target at

The cancellation for n>=1 is in the integral polynomial ring; n=0 gives 2u

namespace MathGKM.Markov

def ambientFormB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x : R) : Mat16 R :=
 ⟨1+x,-x,-x,x⟩

theorem ambient_common_formB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x y : R) (r : Bool) :
 mm16 (ambientFormB5 x) (ambientT5c x y r)=
 if r then ⟨y+x*y^2,x*y,x*y,x⟩ else ⟨x*y,0,0,x⟩ := by
 cases r <;> apply Mat16.ext <;> simp [ambientFormB5,ambientT5c,mm16] <;> ring

def ambientQuadB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x y : R) (w : List Bool)
 (p q : R) : R :=
 let m := ambientWord5c x y w
 ((1+x)*p-x*q)*(m.a*p+m.b*q)+x*(q-p)*(m.c*p+m.d*q)

theorem ambient_word_appendB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x y : R)
 (w z : List Bool) :
 ambientWord5c x y (w++z)=mm16 (ambientWord5c x y w) (ambientWord5c x y z) := by
 induction w with
 | nil => simp [ambientWord5c,mm_one_left774]
 | cons r rs ih => simp only [List.cons_append,ambientWord5c,ih,mm_assoc16]

theorem ambient_quad_sandwichB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x y p q : R)
 (w : List Bool) (r : Bool) :

# Global cut partitions for the ambient transfer

Machine-authored live request a27f6d422b1a478c976694b9ca5c9a54. No novelty
claim. Full published Conjecture63 remains unresolved. Only final successful
validation receipts count as formal evidence.

For a word w, use the inherited positive ambient transfer
T_r=D_r+x c_r H, where H=(1,1)^T(y,1), c_A=1, c_B=1+y,
D_A=[[0,0],[0,1]], and D_B=[[y,0],[2y,1]]. Append one B to w.
The inherited scalar is exactly (y,1) T_(wB) (0,1)^T.

The first row (p,q) has two possible transitions at a position:

* Skip: (p,q)D_A=(0,q), or (p,q)D_B=(y(p+2q),q).
* Select: multiply by x c_r(p+q), then reset the row to (y,1).

Let C(y,p,q;w;s) count exactly s selected positions with these weights.
For the empty word C(0)=q and C(s+1)=0. At r followed by v,

    C(y,p,q;rv;0)=C(y,d_r(p,q),q;v;0),
    C(y,p,q;rv;s+1)=C(y,d_r(p,q),q;v;s+1)
                    +c_r(p+q) C(y,y,1;v;s).

MarkovCutPartitionA27 proves universally that this is the ordinary x
coefficient of the transfer scalar. It proves the zero count C(...;0)=q,
vanishing above the word length, and scalar nonnegativity for nonnegative
real inputs. The latter is explicitly scalar nonnegativity, not an assertion
that pointwise positivity alone implies coefficientwise positivity.

For every actual source path, every natural i,j,s with i+j=a+s, the checked
bridge is

    A(i,j)=[y^j] C(y,y,1;central(path) B;s).

There is no cutoff, normalization, specialization y=1, or suppressed zero.
MarkovCutRootA27 extends this to every original grid position by returning zero
when i+j<a, and proves this is the actual raw coefficient there too. Its
root_iff_cutA27 is an exact equivalence with all three original inequalities
and their three polygon guards. Neither side of this equivalence is proved.

## Explicit gap weights

Write p_u for the first row entry after skipping a gap u, starting at (y,1),
and R(u)=p_u+1. Selecting positions k_1<...<k_s in wB contributes the product
of c_(k_h) R(gap_h); the unselected suffix after the last position contributes
1. For zero selected positions the contribution is 1. This subset description
is the direct expansion of the checked select/skip recursion. The explicit
finite-subset sum is independently tested in Python; it is not a separately
formalized Finset identity.

The universally checked gap formulas are

    R(B^q)=1+2(y+...+y^q)+y^(q+1),
    R(u A B^q)=1+2(y+...+y^q).

Thus a gap weight depends only on its trailing B run and whether the gap is
pure B. In particular its coefficient list is [1,2,...,2,1] or [1,2,...,2].
The q=0 cases are included: the empty gap has weight 1+y, and a gap ending
in A has weight 1. MarkovCutGapsA27 proves these over every commutative ring.

There is no uniform sign for splitting a gap. If alpha_v is the skipped
first-state output starting at (1,0), and beta_v that starting at (0,1),
the checked identity is

    R(u)R(v)-(1+y)R(uv)=(p_u-y)(1+beta_v-alpha_v).

For u=v=A this equals -y; for u=B,v=A it equals y+y^2. This rules out both
unconditional signs for this particular local split comparison, without
refuting a global sum inequality or a source-specific comparison.

## Experiments and obstructions

The independent subset expansion matched all 511 words of length at most 8,
enumerating 174762 subsets. It found the column triple [20,14,10] for
w=BAB^5, at s=1 and j=2,3,4. MarkovCutObstructionA27 proves the exact
univariate slice 8+20y+20y^2+14y^3+10y^4+6y^5+2y^6 and 14^2<20*10.
The virtual label is reduced 7/9, and all three original positions
(6,2),(5,3),(4,4) lie in that polygon. The word is not a palindrome, and
the checked source-central-palindrome theorem proves it cannot be the central
word of any source path. This is an obstruction to arbitrary-word diagonal
closure, not a refutation of the pinned root. Earlier research already records
arbitrary-word diagonal failures; no discovery priority is claimed.

The initial transfer experiment changed states to h=g-f, for which
A maps (f,h) to (x((1+y)f+h),f+h), and B maps it to
((y+x(1+y)^2)f+x(1+y)h,(1+y)f+h). These are positive updates and
F=(1+y)f+h, but their mixed horizontal gap is negative already for source
1/3 at s=j=0. This rejects that termwise route; the total gap is nonnegative.
The 1023 arbitrary words and 627 source fractions in positive-state-probe.json
also distinguish failures of arbitrary-word components from source results.

For the original (yf,g) decomposition, polygon-guarded tests covered 8191

/-- Cross inequalities include ordinary adjacent log-concavity, and keep zeros. -/
def CrossLC (f : ℤ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i ≤ j → f i * f (j+1) ≤ f (i+1) * f j

def Smooth (f : ℤ → ℝ) (k : ℤ) : ℝ := f k + f (k-1)

theorem crossLC_shift {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) (s : ℤ) :
    CrossLC (fun k => f (k+s)) := by
  intro i j hij
  simpa [add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using h (i+s) (j+s) (by omega)

theorem crossLC_forward {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) :
    CrossLC (fun k => f k + f (k+1)) := by
  intro i j hij
  by_cases he : i = j
  · subst j; simp [mul_comm]
  have h1 := h i j hij
  have h2 := h (i+1) (j+1) (by omega)
  have h3 := h i (j+1) (by omega)
  have h4 := h (i+1) j (by omega)
  dsimp only
  nlinarith

theorem crossLC_smooth {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) : CrossLC (Smooth f) := by
  have hs := crossLC_shift (crossLC_forward h) (-1)
  simpa [CrossLC, Smooth, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hs

def Pascal : ℕ → (ℤ → ℝ) → (ℤ → ℝ)
  | 0, f => f
  | n+1, f => Smooth (Pascal n f)

theorem crossLC_pascal {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) (n : ℕ) :
    CrossLC (Pascal n f) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact h
  | succ n ih => exact crossLC_smooth ih

theorem crossLC_adjacent {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) (k : ℤ) :
    f (k-1) * f (k+1) ≤ f k ^ 2 := by
  simpa [sq] using h (k-1) k (by omega)

def QuadSeq (A B C : ℝ) (k : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  if k=0 then A else if k=1 then B else if k=2 then C else 0

theorem quad_nonneg {A B C : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (k : ℤ) : 0 ≤ QuadSeq A B C k := by
  unfold QuadSeq; split_ifs <;> first | assumption | exact le_rfl

theorem crossLC_quad {A B C : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : A*C ≤ B^2) : CrossLC (QuadSeq A B C) := by
  intro i j hij
  by_cases hi : 0 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ 2
  · by_cases hj : -1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ 1
    · obtain ⟨hi0,hi2⟩ := hi
      obtain ⟨hj0,hj1⟩ := hj
      interval_cases i <;> interval_cases j <;> norm_num [QuadSeq] at * <;> nlinarith
    · have hz : QuadSeq A B C (j+1) = 0 := by
        simp only [QuadSeq]; split_ifs <;> first | omega | rfl
      rw [hz, mul_zero]
      exact mul_nonneg (quad_nonneg hA hB hC _) (quad_nonneg hA hB hC _)
  · have hz : QuadSeq A B C i = 0 := by
      simp only [QuadSeq]; split_ifs <;> first | omega | rfl
    rw [hz, zero_mul]
    exact mul_nonneg (quad_nonneg hA hB hC _) (quad_nonneg hA hB hC _)

theorem quadratic_pascal_logConcave {A B C : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : A*C ≤ B^2) (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ) :
    Pascal n (QuadSeq A B C) (k-1) * Pascal n (QuadSeq A B C) (k+1) ≤
      Pascal n (QuadSeq A B C) k ^ 2 :=
  crossLC_adjacent (crossLC_pascal (crossLC_quad hA hB hC h) n) k

open Polynomial

/-- Polynomial coefficients extended by zero at negative integer indices. -/
def CoeffSeq (p : ℝ[X]) (k : ℤ) : ℝ := if k < 0 then 0 else p.coeff k.toNat

theorem coeffSeq_smooth (p : ℝ[X]) :
    CoeffSeq ((1+X)*p) = Smooth (CoeffSeq p) := by
  funext k
  by_cases hk : k < 0
  · have hk' : k-1 < 0 := by omega
    simp [CoeffSeq, Smooth, hk, hk']
  · have hk0 : 0 ≤ k := by omega
    lift k to ℕ using hk0
    cases k with
    | zero => simp [CoeffSeq, Smooth, add_mul]
    | succ n =>
      simp [CoeffSeq, Smooth, add_mul,
        show ¬ (↑n + 1 : ℤ) < 0 by omega,
        show ¬ (↑n : ℤ) < 0 by omega]

def Quadratic (A B D : ℝ) : ℝ[X] := C A + C B * X + C D * X^2

theorem coeffSeq_quadratic (A B D : ℝ) :
    CoeffSeq (Quadratic A B D) = QuadSeq A B D := by
  funext k
  by_cases hk : k < 0
  · simp [CoeffSeq, QuadSeq, hk, show k ≠ 0 by omega,
      show k ≠ 1 by omega, show k ≠ 2 by omega]
  · lift k to ℕ using (show 0 ≤ k by omega)
    by_cases h0 : k = 0
    · subst k; norm_num [CoeffSeq, Quadratic, QuadSeq]
    by_cases h1 : k = 1
    · subst k; norm_num [CoeffSeq, Quadratic, QuadSeq]
    by_cases h2 : k = 2
    · subst k
      change (Quadratic A B D).coeff 2 = D
      simp [Quadratic]
    simp [CoeffSeq, Quadratic, QuadSeq, coeff_X, coeff_C, h0, h1, h2, Ne.symm h1,
      show ¬ (↑k : ℤ) < 0 by omega, show (↑k : ℤ) ≠ 2 by omega]

theorem coeffSeq_binomial_mul (p : ℝ[X]) (n : ℕ) :
    CoeffSeq ((1+X)^n*p) = Pascal n (CoeffSeq p) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [Pascal]
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [pow_succ', mul_assoc, coeffSeq_smooth, ih]
    rfl

theorem quadratic_binomial_logConcave {A B D : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (h : A*D ≤ B^2) (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ) :
    let f := CoeffSeq ((1+X)^n * Quadratic A B D)
    f (k-1) * f (k+1) ≤ f k ^ 2 := by
  dsimp only
  rw [coeffSeq_binomial_mul, coeffSeq_quadratic]
  exact quadratic_pascal_logConcave hA hB hD h n k

def ThirdA (a : ℝ) := (a-1)*(a-2)/2
def ThirdB (a b : ℝ) := a*b-4*a+2
def ThirdC (b : ℝ) := (b-1)*(b-2)/2

/-- Certificate selected after the exact experiment, not a sampled inequality. -/
theorem third_gap_certificate (t s : ℝ) :
    4 * (ThirdB (t+3) (t+s+4)^2 - ThirdA (t+3) * ThirdC (t+s+4)) =
      4 + 38*s + 34*s^2 + 20*t + 69*t*s + 21*t*s^2 +
      29*t^2 + 37*t^2*s + 3*t^2*s^2 + 16*t^3 + 6*t^3*s + 3*t^4 := by
  unfold ThirdA ThirdB ThirdC
  ring

theorem third_parameters {a b : ℝ} (ha : 3 ≤ a) (hb : a+1 ≤ b) :
    0 ≤ ThirdA a ∧ 0 ≤ ThirdB a b ∧ 0 ≤ ThirdC b ∧
      ThirdA a * ThirdC b ≤ ThirdB a b ^ 2 := by
  have ht : 0 ≤ a-3 := by linarith
  have hs : 0 ≤ b-a-1 := by linarith
  have he := third_gap_certificate (a-3) (b-a-1)
  have ea : a-3+3 = a := by ring
  have eb : a-3+(b-a-1)+4 = b := by ring
  rw [ea, eb] at he
  have hp : 0 ≤ 4 + 38*(b-a-1) + 34*(b-a-1)^2 + 20*(a-3) +
      69*(a-3)*(b-a-1) + 21*(a-3)*(b-a-1)^2 + 29*(a-3)^2 +
      37*(a-3)^2*(b-a-1) + 3*(a-3)^2*(b-a-1)^2 + 16*(a-3)^3 +
      6*(a-3)^3*(b-a-1) + 3*(a-3)^4 := by positivity
  have hA : 0 ≤ ThirdA a := by
    unfold ThirdA
    exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)) (by norm_num)
  have hC : 0 ≤ ThirdC b := by
    have : 3 ≤ b := by linarith
    unfold ThirdC
    exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)) (by norm_num)
  have hB : 0 ≤ ThirdB a b := by
    have hprod : 0 ≤ a*(b-a-1) := mul_nonneg (by linarith) hs
    have hprod2 : 0 ≤ (a-1)*(a-2) := mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)
    unfold ThirdB
    nlinarith
  exact ⟨hA,hB,hC,by nlinarith⟩

/-- All coefficients of the published third-diagonal expression, with no
restriction a/b<=3/5. This theorem is about the explicit polynomial;
the recurrence-to-expression identity is a separate formal obligation. -/
theorem third_diagonal_expression_logConcave (a b : ℕ) (ha : 3 ≤ a) (hab : a < b)
    (k : ℤ) :
    let f := CoeffSeq ((1+X)^(a+b-5) *
      Quadratic (ThirdA a) (ThirdB a b) (ThirdC b))
    f (k-1) * f (k+1) ≤ f k ^ 2 := by
  have h := third_parameters (a := (a:ℝ)) (b := (b:ℝ))
    (by exact_mod_cast ha) (by exact_mod_cast hab)
  exact quadratic_binomial_logConcave h.1 h.2.1 h.2.2.1 h.2.2.2 _ _

/-- Literal algebraic form of the source's T₂ at v=1, with n=a+b-5. -/
def SourceThird (a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ[X] :=
  C (ThirdA a)*(1+X)^(n+2) + C (a*(b-a)-a)*X*(1+X)^(n+1) +
    C (((b-a)^2+5*a-3*b)/2)*X^2*(1+X)^n

theorem sourceThird_factor (a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    SourceThird a b n = (1+X)^n * Quadratic (ThirdA a) (ThirdB a b) (ThirdC b) := by
  have hB : ThirdB a b = 2*ThirdA a+(a*(b-a)-a) := by
    unfold ThirdB ThirdA; ring
  have hC : ThirdC b = ThirdA a+(a*(b-a)-a)+((b-a)^2+5*a-3*b)/2 := by
    unfold ThirdC ThirdA; ring
  rw [hB,hC]
  simp only [SourceThird, Quadratic, pow_add, pow_one, map_add, map_mul, map_ofNat]
  ring

def DiagonalSeq (P : BiPoly) (d : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  if 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ d then (coeff P k.toNat (d-k.toNat) : ℝ) else 0

/-- Explicit remaining formula bridge. This is a proposition, not an axiom. -/
def ThirdDiagonalFormula (l : Label) : Prop :=
  DiagonalSeq l.p (l.a+l.b-3) = CoeffSeq (SourceThird l.a l.b (l.a+l.b-5))

/-- Honest conditional transfer to the actual raw Markov diagonal. -/
theorem third_diagonal_of_formula (l : Label) (ha : 3 ≤ l.a) (hab : l.a < l.b)
    (hf : ThirdDiagonalFormula l) (k : ℤ) :
    DiagonalSeq l.p (l.a+l.b-3) (k-1) * DiagonalSeq l.p (l.a+l.b-3) (k+1) ≤
      DiagonalSeq l.p (l.a+l.b-3) k ^ 2 := by
  unfold ThirdDiagonalFormula at hf
  rw [hf, sourceThird_factor]
  exact third_diagonal_expression_logConcave l.a l.b ha hab k

# Horizontal sector obstruction in a literal source row

Machine-authored research, request f93ee68f6b414a928b23bb07728597c4.
This is not a resolution of the pinned Conjecture63. Final build and replay
status is recorded separately in evidence/markov-f93ee68f/validation.json.

The fixed-charge matching agenda did not yield a new injection or inequality.
A different sufficient strategy was tested: factor each horizontal polynomial
into linear factors and quadratic factors whose own raw coefficients are LC.
Nonreal roots of a real quadratic a+bX+cX² with ac<=b² obey
Im(z)²<=3 Re(z)². Thus a source root violating this inequality obstructs that
factorization strategy, even though the source's coefficient sequence can be LC.

Take the actual protected frame at List.replicate 22 true. Its label is 23/24.
The horizontal row j=26 has degree 20 and coefficients, starting at i=0:

    231, 18970, 790020, 21380814, 411390021, 5877864648,

row, using the inherited exact raw Pell coefficient formula and zero cases.

including indices beyond the support. Its polygon on this row is exactly
0<=i<=20. Thus the sector obstruction is explicitly NOT a raw LC failure.

## Exact complex root certificate

The root lies in the radius-1/10000 disk about an explicitly recorded rational
complex center approximately

    -0.02823064230705693446 - 0.05087697677069144583 i.

sector-certificate.json. Exact rational Horner evaluation bounds |Re P(c)|+
|Im P(c)| strictly below (1/10000)^20. No floating-point assertion enters the
proof. The general certificate in MarkovRootCertificateF93e uses factorization
over C: if every root were at distance at least r, then

    |P(c)| = |leadingCoefficient| product_roots |c-z|
           >= |leadingCoefficient| r^degree.

The strict reverse bound therefore supplies an actual root in the disk.
Elementary rational bounds on the entire disk imply Re z<0 and
3(Re z)^2<(Im z)^2. This is outside the closed 120-degree sector centered on
the negative real axis. The initial numerical approximation only selected the
rational center; the formal proof checks the residual and existence directly.

MarkovQuadraticObstructionF93e gives the precise factorization obstruction.
For any real a,b,c, not all zero, with ac<=b², a complex number satisfying
Im(z)²>3 Re(z)² cannot annihilate a+bz+cz². Taking imaginary and real parts
forces b=-2c Re(z) and a=c(Re(z)²+Im(z)²), contradicting ac<=b² when c≠0;
c=0 forces all coefficients zero. Therefore the actual source row is not a
finite product of such nonzero real linear/quadratic factors. This statement
even omits nonnegativity assumptions on the factors, making the obstruction
stronger. It excludes a specific sufficient proof route, not more general
factorizations or direct coefficient arguments.

The first numerical scan considered 6175 nonconstant stripped slice polynomials
through denominator 20. It found vertical and diagonal sector violations; no
horizontal violation occurred in that finite range. The subsequent source
scan with bound 45 was time-capped after 194 source polynomials and 6275 rows;
it is NOT complete coverage through denominator 45. One row exceeded the
numerical residual tolerance and is marked unreliable.

horizontal candidates outside the sector; two numerical rows were unreliable.
Those enlarged words are not asserted to belong to the source family.
The targeted Pell scan located the exact-source candidate above. Every
numerical result remains experimental; only explicitly checked Lean theorems
receive theorem status. No universal claim follows from any scan.

https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html .
Hosted literature search found no applicable general proof of the fixed-charge
fiber goal. Sector-stability and matching references were exploratory only;
no external assertion was introduced as an axiom. No novelty claim is made.

theorem choose_upper_lc6 (n k : ℕ) :

        Nat.cast_add,Nat.cast_one] using h

      have h := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => (x:ℤ)) (Nat.choose_mul_succ_eq (n+1) k)
      have he : n+1+1=n+2 := by omega
      rw [he] at h
      simpa only [Nat.cast_mul,Nat.cast_sub (show k≤n+2 by omega),
        Nat.cast_add,Nat.cast_one,Nat.cast_ofNat] using h
    have hn : (0:ℤ)<n+1 := by omega
    have hm : (0:ℤ)<n+2-k := by omega

# Exact support, mechanical words, and strategy obstructions

Machine-authored request 3edac4bf4f1040d0b967711f6c52c66f. Validation status is
recorded by source hash in evidence/markov-3edac4bf/validation.json. None of
these results proves or refutes the full pinned Conjecture63.

## Saturation from exact prefix counts

Write a,b for a source middle label and W for its raw A/B word, of length b
with a copies of B. The inherited support-rigidity proof identified proper
central prefix counts. MarkovMechanical3eda extends this to the entire word:

    count_B(take j W) = floor(a*j/b),    0 <= j <= b.

The j=0,b-1,b endpoint cases are explicitly checked, using 0<a<b. The exact
raw-word/source polynomial identity is also recorded, without normalization.

For 0<j<b, split W=x r y with length(x)=j-1. The inherited positive matrix
path witness gives a positive coefficient at

    (count_B(y), length(x)+indicator(r=B)).

Its second coordinate is at most j. If q=count_B(take j W), then a=q+count_B(y)
and a*j < b*(q+1). At any polygon point (i,j), the inequality
a*b <= b*i+a*j therefore forces count_B(y)<=i. The inherited northeast
support propagation reaches (i,j), since i+j<=a+b-1. For j=0 use the positive
vertex (a,0); for j>=b use (0,b). This proves source_saturated3eda for every
finite path and every polygon lattice point, with no bound on a or b.

Combining it with the existing outside-zero theorem gives exactly

    0 < A_ij iff InPolygon(a,b,i,j),
    A_ij = 0 iff not InPolygon(a,b,i,j).

This is stronger than convex-hull equality or interval support: every polygon
lattice point has a nonzero raw coefficient. It does not compare coefficient
magnitudes. Saturation is already a known mathematical result; the primary
paper [Evans, Saturation of Markov Polynomials](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.18333v1)
was retrieved live. This run uses a checked matrix-word argument, not an external
theorem as an axiom, and makes no historical novelty claim.

## An explicit arithmetic root formulation

Define the length-b word by its kth letter:

    W(a,b)[k] = B if floor(a*k/b) < floor(a*(k+1)/b), else A.

MarkovMechanicalGoal3eda proves exact equality with each source word by taking
successive prefix-count differences. Conversely rational_coverage_098 supplies
an actual source path for every positive reduced a<b, with literal polynomial
equality to the raw matrix product of W(a,b).

root_iff_mechanical3eda equates the full pinned root with GlobalLC18 for all
these explicit words. There is no support condition or unknown family bridge
on this new target. Both sides remain unproved. The equivalence retains the
three raw directions, all indices and zeros, and uses the inherited vacuous
0/1 and 1/1 endpoint clauses through root_iff_raw_matrix18.

## All diagonal support and cross inequalities

For every n define D_n(k)=A_{k,n-k} when 0<=k<=n, and zero otherwise. Saturation
and the linear polygon inequalities give interval support for every D_n,
including lower diagonals. Together with nonnegativity, the inherited adjacent
to CrossLC theorem applies without a no-gap premise. MarkovCrossGoal3eda glues
this to the analogous horizontal and vertical results into a full-root
equivalence with CrossLC on every raw slice. Neither inequality side is proved.
This concerns raw slices; it does not claim log-concavity of quotient slices
or invert the smoothing transform.
